subject: NexaHealth — no-model-improvement commitment & response ownership path
messages:
From: Liz Sanders <liz.sanders@nexahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nexahealth.com
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: contract ask — no-model-improve + response ownership

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — product looks promising. Procurement and legal at NexaHealth asked me to get clarity on two items before we move to PO: a firm commitment that customer interactions will not be used to improve upstream models ("no-model-improvement"), and confirmation of how output/response IP is handled (we need explicit assignment or license to the responses produced from our prompts).

Specific asks:
- Contract language that prevents use of our interactions for model training or fine-tuning (not just anonymized telemetry).
- A technical description of the operational controls you can implement (e.g., dedicated model instance, per-customer KV isolation, customer-managed keys, explicit log retention periods).
- An evidence pack (SOC2 + architecture note) showing where and how subprocessor access is restricted.

We really like Redwood but because Nexa handles PHI-adjacent data, these items are gating. Can you propose a path we can commit to in the DPA?

Thanks,
Liz
Liz Sanders
Head of Procurement, NexaHealth
liz.sanders@nexahealth.com

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Sanders <liz.sanders@nexahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 11:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: contract ask — no-model-improve + response ownership

Hi Liz — really appreciate the clear checklist. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Jonas (product infra) to propose concrete contract language and operational controls.

High level — we can offer three complementary levers:
1) Contractual: a DPA addendum that prohibits use of customer-supplied data for model training or improvement (no-model-improvement), with defined exceptions (operational telemetry for availability/uptime only).
2) Technical: options include (a) dedicated model deployment pinned to your account, (b) ephemeral-session inference (KV cache never persisted beyond session TTL), (c) customer-managed KMS for keys used in any encryption-at-rest, and (d) explicit prompt/response export rights.
3) Operational evidence: SOC2 Type II, subprocessor inventory, and an "Isolation Controls" appendix describing who can access logs and the retention windows.

Marissa/Jonas — can you draft the DPA redline + a short controls matrix we can send to Nexa today? Liz, if you have an internal template or preferred redline, please attach.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Liz Sanders <liz.sanders@nexahealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: contract ask — no-model-improve + response ownership

Hi Liz — thanks for the note. I reviewed the request and attached a working redline (NexaHealth_DPA_redlines_20260401.docx) that:
- Adds an explicit clause: "Provider will not use Customer Content to train, update, or improve Provider models" and defines "Customer Content" to include prompts and system instructions.
- Provides operational carveouts: allowed telemetry (for availability, abuse detection) will be aggregated and cannot be used for model training.
- Includes an evidence deliverable: a one-time architecture note plus quarterly attestations around subprocessors and KMS custody.

Jonas — please add a 1-page technical appendix describing: ephemeral-prefix hashing, session-only KV cache behavior, and the option to run a pinned model variant for Nexa.

Liz — quick questions for your team to close the redline:
1) Are you okay with "quarterly attestations" (short note + current subprocessor list) rather than continuous audit access?
2) Do you require onshore (US) data residency for all logs/telemetry or only for training artifacts (which we will not create)?

If we can get answers on those two points we can update the doc and route for signature.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Liz Sanders <liz.sanders@nexahealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: contract ask — no-model-improve + response ownership

Liz — attaching the short technical appendix we discussed (pasted below). This is intended to be included as an appendix to the DPA, not as part of the main T&C.

--- Technical Appendix (summary) ---
Operational controls we can implement for NexaHealth:
- Dedicated deployment: spin up a pinned model instance with isolated weights and separate KV cache namespace. This prevents cross-tenant mixing by runtime configuration.
- Ephemeral KV + session TTL: KV cache entries (conversation context) exist only for the session and get garbage-collected within configurable TTL (default 24 hours).
- Ephemeral-prefix hashing: prompts are hashed client-side (optional SDK hook) so stored telemetry cannot be easily tied back to raw prompts.
- Customer-managed KMS: we can integrate a customer-managed key for encrypting logs and ephemeral storage; Redwood will not have the plaintext key.
- No-training commitment: we will ensure that no logged data is exported to any model training pipeline; offline metrics (latency, failure rates) may be computed on aggregated, non-content data.

Open technical items for Nexa: whether they need event logs (API calls, response metadata) to be retained onshore and for how long. If Nexa wants logs onshore for all telemetry, we can propose an onshore log retention lane.

Let me know and I will attach the appendix to the DPA redline.

Jonas Weber
Director, Product Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Liz Sanders <liz.sanders@nexahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: contract ask — no-model-improve + response ownership

Thanks — the redline and appendix look good. A couple of clarifications from procurement/legal:
- Quarterly attestations are acceptable as long as they include the current subprocessor snapshot and a signed attestation that no customer content was used for model improvement.
- Nexa requires onshore retention for all event logs containing identifiers for >0.1% of PHI-related transactions — essentially, we want the ability to request an onshore copy of logs if we trigger an audit. Will Redwood commit to a Fed/US log retention lane that can be enabled for our account?
- For response ownership: we need express assignment of output IP for outputs generated from our prompts during the term; a license-back to Redwood for service delivery only is acceptable.

If you can update the DPA with these three bullet points and send the DocuSign link, procurement will aim to sign within 5 business days.

Best,
Liz
Head of Procurement, NexaHealth
